name: Congolese nationalism
summary: Congolese nationalism is the drive to build one sovereign Congolese nation out of a territory the Belgians drew and a population divided into many ethnic groups. Its core, in Patrice Lumumba's tradition, is independence, a unitary centralised state against regionalism and secession, equality and an end to colonial discrimination, economic independence, non-alignment and Pan-African solidarity. Under Mobutu it became the state doctrine of authenticite, stressing cultural return to African heritage and a single leader and party.
scope: Mainstream Lumumbist anti-colonial and unitarist nationalism of 1958-1960 (the independence speech and the MNC platform), which Congolese politicians of every later regime have claimed, plus Mobutu's Zairian authenticite as a strand on culture and religion. Answers on one-party rule and religion are split because the strands differ. It excludes ethnic or regional nationalisms inside the DRC and the Kongo kingdom's historical identity.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Lumumba's humanism saw the state as an active promoter of public welfare, so state-guaranteed health care fits, though no health program is documented.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The independence speech promised fair pay and social justice for workers; a wage floor is an inference from that, not a stated policy.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Lumumba's MNC favoured state-led development and a national economy under Congolese control, which sits against a market-first stance.

public-ownership.rationale: State-led development was part of the MNC platform, but Lumumba also signed a contract with a private US-linked firm, so ownership of utilities is inferred only.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Social justice and economic independence imply redistribution toward Congolese, but taxation of the wealthy is never discussed in the sources.

unions-good.rationale: The speech promises fair treatment for workers; unions are not addressed, so support is inferred from that.

property-fundamental.rationale: Lumumba stressed that the land must serve its own people, which implies property yields to national interest; not discussed directly.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The call for an economy assuring Congolese independence implies control over foreign firms, inferred rather than stated.

cut-welfare.rationale: A state seen as promoter of public welfare is hostile to welfare cuts; inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Lumumbism is described as never a detailed economic doctrine, and nothing in the sources addresses worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; Lumumba's government restricted the press and declared an emergency, but adherents are not documented as taking a side on surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Congolese nationalism has no recorded position on drug policy.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Lumumba urged people to forget tribal quarrels, but no sources show a stance on legally restricting hate speech.

strong-leader.rationale: Lumumba sought a centralised state and Mobutu's authenticité justified a single strong chief; a strong unifying leader is part of the tradition, though Lumumba also worked through parliament.

state-harmful.rationale: The movement is about building and holding a unitary Congolese state; its founders and Mobutu alike saw the state as necessary.

limit-guns.rationale: No documented position on civilian gun ownership.

empower-police-military.rationale: National unity was defended by force against secession in 1960, so a stronger army is inferred, though Lumumba's own army mutinied.

decide-locally.rationale: Lumumba wanted a centralised state to end regionalism and tribalism, and opposed Kasa-Vubu's federalism.

rehabilitation.rationale: No documented position on penal policy.

traditional-family.rationale: Authenticité exalted ancestral heritage and custom, so family tradition is inferred as valued; the sources do not mention the family directly.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Authenticité framed Western ways as alien to ancestral custom; opposition is inferred, not documented.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the cultural-traditionalist strand of authenticité; no source discusses abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: Mobutu's authenticité curbed churches as colonial, while Lumumba, raised Catholic, was not anti-religious, so the two strands in scope split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Lumumba promised an end to discrimination of every variety and denounced the humiliations of colonial rule.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Authenticité was explicitly a return to ancestral heritage and cultural disalienation, a core of the Zairian strand.

gradual-change.rationale: The nationalists demanded independence and a decisive break with colonial order; MNC however favoured gradual Africanisation of the administration.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not documented as an issue in the sources.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Lumumba turned from the UN to other backers when it failed to support him, and prized sovereignty above outside authority.

free-trade.rationale: The economic-independence aim implies national control of trade; free trade is not discussed.

nation-first.rationale: Independence and economic sovereignty were the aim, with aid accepted only if it imposes no outside culture or conditions.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Foreign interference in Congo's affairs was the central grievance; an adherent would oppose outside force even for rights.

open-borders.rationale: Sovereignty over the national territory is central; open borders are inferred as unwelcome.

limit-growth.rationale: Development and a prosperous national economy were goals; degrowth is not discussed.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The sources give no view on technology as a cure for humanity's problems; the nationalist focus was independence and development.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power appears nowhere in the sources on Lumumba or Mobutu, and no position can be inferred from the nationalist principles.

revolution-justified.rationale: Lumumba's speech presents the struggle against colonial rule as just, but he also urged legal opposition afterward.

experts-over-public.rationale: The speech frames the people as sovereign; no technocratic claim is documented.

central-planning.rationale: State-led development is documented, but no commitment to full central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Lumumbism is not a detailed economic doctrine; no stance on market socialism.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land taxation is not discussed in the sources; Lumumba's land concern was national ownership of benefits, not a tax design.

tax-inheritance.rationale: No source describes the movement's view of inheritance taxes, so adherents are not shown to take a side.

basic-income.rationale: An unconditional state payment is not in any documented program, and the MNC platform stressed state-led development instead.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: An economy assuring independence suggests protecting domestic production; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State-led development is part of the MNC platform.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The sources do not say whether the nationalists favoured small owners over the state or firms; Zairianisation and state-led plans point both ways.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: No source describes Congolese nationalists organising labour into state bodies, though the Mobutu regime later controlled unions.

one-party-rule.rationale: Mobutu built a single-party state, claiming Africans never have two chiefs, while Lumumba worked through parliament and accepted opposition, so the strands split.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The movement was built around a republic; no monarchist tradition is documented, and Belgian monarchy was the colonial crown.

democracy-best.rationale: Lumumba pledged consent and liberty, yet his government restricted the press and Mobutu's authenticité rejected multiparty politics; adherents split.

direct-votes.rationale: Referendums on laws are not part of the documented Lumumbist or Mobutist programs, which worked through parliament or a party.

workers-councils.rationale: Lumumba worked through parliament; councils as the basis of power are not part of the tradition.

right-to-secede.rationale: Lumumba wanted a centralised state and fought Katanga and Kasai secession; national unity is called his greatest legacy.

natural-rulers.rationale: Mobutu spoke of a single chief by African tradition, but no doctrine of natural rulers is documented.

political-violence-never.rationale: The nationalists presented the anti-colonial struggle as legitimate, while Lumumba spoke of a peace not of guns and bayonets.

war-builds-character.rationale: The speech prizes peace of the heart and the will; no glorification of war is documented.

separate-church-state.rationale: Mobutu's regime clashed with the churches while Lumumba's government held no separation doctrine, so the strands split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: No scriptural law is part of the doctrine; authenticité was the opposite, a national cultural basis.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The movement centres on a strong sovereign state that holds the army and courts.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Congolese nationalism is an effort to build one nation out of many ethnic groups, and Lumumba told people to forget tribal quarrels.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Lumumba's humanism stressed social harmony and unity over class conflict, and the movement is framed as national, not Marxist.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Egalitarianism and social justice are noted for Lumumba, but equality of outcomes is not specified.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The speech speaks of land protected for Congolese as a nation, not for indigenous groups within it; the question fits poorly.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The speech describes eighty years of forced labour and humiliation, and the nation made claims on Belgium, but explicit reparations demands are not in the sources.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-African union is documented, but it is continental rather than religion or civilization-based.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The movement's ethos is national solidarity and social justice rather than individual self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Authenticité stressed community and the leader, but Lumumba promised basic liberties; split.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is absent from the sources on Congolese nationalism.

limit-population.rationale: Population control is not discussed in the sources; the speech presents poverty as a colonial legacy.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The nationalist goal was development and prosperity; rejection of industry is not part of it.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Speeding up technology despite institutional disruption is not addressed in the sources, and the movement's focus was building new national institutions.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bodily enhancement is outside anything the sources attribute to the nationalists.

algorithmic-government.rationale: AI in government is anachronistic for a 1960 movement and the sources give no basis for a position.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption is anachronistic and absent from the sources, so no stance is inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: The nationalists sought a new independent order; authenticité drew on heritage but also aimed at a modern unified nation.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Lumumba's positive neutralism was pragmatic in foreign policy, but the sources do not show a general judge-by-results stance.

direct-action.rationale: Anti-colonial riots in 1959 were nationalist direct action, yet the MNC also worked through elections and parliament.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources do not say whether the nationalists held that means must mirror ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Development and a prosperous economy are explicit goals of the movement.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not addressed; the program favoured state-led development of a modern economy.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Social justice is promised but communist distribution is not documented as an aim.

production-for-use.rationale: No documented stance on profit versus use.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The speech condemns colonial exploitation of labour, but not profit as such.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Lumumba's movement was a national, not working-class, front and he pursued parliamentary government.

collective-farming.rationale: Not documented; Zairianisation transferred property to individuals rather than collectives.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Anti-imperialism is central, but no theory tying capitalism to wars is documented.

taxation-theft.rationale: A state-led development movement needs revenue; the claim runs against its view of the state.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberal limits on state power are not documented; Lumumba promised liberties yet his government restricted the press, so adherents are split.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Authenticité put the community and nation above the individual; the sources do not address group rights directly.

conscription.rationale: A national army defending unity is implied, but conscription is not documented.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition values national loyalty over exit.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is seen as promoter of welfare and development, not as a firm.

positive-liberty.rationale: The speech links freedom to social justice and economic independence; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: No source records the nationalists blaming universities or media for holding political power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Lumumba rejected racial hierarchy and promised to end discrimination of every kind.

organic-representation.rationale: Authenticité had corporatist traits in the one-party state, but the sources do not describe family-based representation.

total-state.rationale: Authenticité reshaped names, dress and culture under the state, while Lumumbism had no such aim, so the strands split.

national-rebirth.rationale: Authenticité called for a return to authenticity and cultural disalienation after colonial damage.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The movement's priority was holding the inherited colonial territory, not expanding it.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not an element of the doctrine.

bound-labor.rationale: The speech condemns forced labour under colonial rule.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Authenticité's mental decolonization hints at it, but no epistemic claim is documented.

universal-morality.rationale: The sources do not say whether the nationalists held universal rational moral truths; authenticité leaned to cultural particularity, Lumumba to humanist universals.

single-common-good.rationale: A single rationally discovered common good is not a documented doctrine, though national unity was treated as the shared aim.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: No source gives a Congolese nationalist position.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return is not a theme in the sources on Congolese nationalism.

revive-national-language.rationale: Authenticité promoted African names, though not revival of a dead language; Lingala and Swahili were already in use.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Worker votes on company management are not in the documented MNC platform, which stressed state-led development.

school-vouchers.rationale: State welfare orientation suggests public schooling; inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The sources contain no fiscal policy position by the nationalists on deficits.

economic-freedom.rationale: Split between state-led development and the open economy; not addressed directly.

rule-by-example.rationale: Mobutu cast himself as father of the nation, but no doctrine of rule by example is stated.

national-self-determination.rationale: The independence speech and the whole movement affirm the Congolese right to govern themselves in their own state.

force-without-un.rationale: Lumumba pursued UN help, but no general doctrine on force abroad exists.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The sources give no stance; Lumumba was raised Catholic and authenticité revered ancestral tradition, so adherents do not share one rule.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility for immigrants is not discussed in the sources.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Work requirements for welfare are not addressed in the sources on the movement.

class-collaboration.rationale: Lumumba's humanism favoured social harmony and national unity over class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Authenticité valued ancestral heritage and cultural preservation.

dominated-front.rationale: Lumumba pursued positive neutralism and non-alignment with other African and anti-colonial states.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism took precedence, but no worker nationalism doctrine.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury bans are not part of the documented nationalist program.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The speech rejects racial discrimination and the unequal treatment of colonial rule.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Not addressed beyond the Red Africa framing.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Oil, gas and coal policy is not covered in the sources, which stress national control of the economy generally.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Authenticité sought a single national identity, but its stance on immigrants is not documented.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not part of any documented nationalism and contrary to its unity project.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral system design is not documented for Lumumba's MNC or Mobutu's party state.

national-mission.rationale: The nationalism was defensive and anti-colonial, not proselytising.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Feminist analysis of patriarchy is not part of the sources on Congolese nationalism.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Lumumbists denounced colonial collaborators, but corruption in this sense is not documented as a doctrine.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Contradicts the humanist egalitarianism of the speech.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The speech promised an end to suppression and respect for liberty; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state is seen as an active promoter of welfare and development.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Lumumba promised an end to all discrimination and framed Congolese and Belgians as equal and independent.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Congolese nationalism is not a socialist doctrine, so the debate over socialism in one country does not apply to it.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed directly; colonial borders were criticised but settler-state status is not.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: A unitary national identity over ethnic divisions suggests equal law, though not documented.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Mobutu restricted non-recognised churches, but no stance on conversion is documented.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Religious cattle protection is irrelevant to the sources on Congolese nationalism.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Authenticité conflicted with mission schools, but the sources do not give a school doctrine.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This is a Marxist-Leninist debate; Congolese nationalism is not tied to it in the sources.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Lumumba promised rule by consent, not by the peace of guns and bayonets.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export surplus is not discussed; the speech stresses economic independence, not trade balances.

population-transfer.rationale: Contradicts unity and equality; the movement sought to include all peoples in the nation.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Libertarian non-aggression is not in the sources; Lumumba's government itself used force against secessionists.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The movement stressed unity and cooperation over struggle.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Lumumba's government banned unsanctioned associations; split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The anti-colonial concern with being ruled by others fits this idea; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Lumumba worked through parliament but Mobutu concentrated power; split.

vanguard-party.rationale: The MNC aimed to be a national front, not a vanguard of a class.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Social justice and egalitarianism are noted for Lumumba.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: British-style social housing sales have no counterpart in the sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law is not discussed, though the speech promised fair treatment of workers.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The speech attributes poverty to colonial exploitation, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Congolese nationalism is an attempt to build cohesion across many ethnic groups.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Selection by lot runs against the elected, parliamentary government Lumumba led, though the sources do not discuss it directly.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Lumumba's government declared a state of emergency and Mobutu ruled by decree, but neither strand states a doctrine on emergency powers, so the answer is contested.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price caps on food are not documented, though a state promoting welfare might support them.

party-controls-media.rationale: Mobutu's party controlled the press, while Lumumba's brief government only restricted it under criticism, so the strands split.

party-commands-army.rationale: Mobutu's MPR dominated the state, but no doctrine is documented.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization rules are not addressed in the sources on Congolese nationalism.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay for representatives is not discussed in the sources.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: MNC and MPR discipline not documented.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Lumumba agreed on a Union of African States with Nkrumah, but defended Congolese sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Lumumba and Kasa-Vubu clashed over control of the army.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is outside the nationalist program; Mobutu regulated churches but did not prescribe their internal structure.

clerical-rule.rationale: The movement is secular-national and Mobutu curbed church power.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism is a Leninist doctrine absent from the sources on Congolese nationalism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Censorship of art for moral reasons is not documented in the sources, although the Mobutu regime did control culture.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Mobutu stayed in power indefinitely, but this was not a doctrine.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall votes are not discussed in the sources on Lumumba or authenticité.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Positive neutralism and non-alignment imply keeping out of permanent blocs.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The sources contain no housing doctrine; mandatory home ownership is unlikely for adherents.

people-in-arms.rationale: Lumumba wanted a national army under state control.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Authenticité valued heritage, but no rural-moral claim is documented.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Congolese nationalism accepts colonial borders; it does not seek reunification of divided peoples.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The sources do not record nationalists blaming educated elites; Lumumba himself was a self-taught evolué.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Authenticité held African culture on par with the West and sought cultural disalienation.

death-penalty.rationale: The death penalty is not discussed in the sources; Mobutu used it but it was not a stated doctrine.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: School sex education is not mentioned in the sources on the movement.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Teaching creationism is not in any source on Congolese nationalism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Pornography law is not mentioned in the sources.

minority-language-support.rationale: The sources stress one national identity across ethnic groups but do not state a policy on minority-language schooling.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions for religious minorities are not addressed; Mobutu's regime banned unrecognised churches, but Lumumba made no such rule.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill-style individuality is absent from the sources; authenticité urged national conformity in dress and names.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Economic independence implies hostility to foreign financial control; debt is not discussed.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The speech calls for a prosperous national economy that assures economic independence as completing political independence.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Rewriting the constitution through an elected assembly is not documented for the nationalist movement.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Mobutu justified authoritarian rule by unity and development; Lumumba did not.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The speech welcomes foreign aid so long as it is freely given and imposes no outside culture.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons are not mentioned in the sources on Congolese nationalism.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The sources do not say how heads of state should be chosen; in 1960 the parliament chose Kasa-Vubu.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Economic sovereignty implies national control; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial integrity was defended against Katanga and Kasai secession, though that case differs from conceding land abroad.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The speech says the land must serve the national interest.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The character of the USSR is not a Congolese nationalist question in the sources, though Lumumba sought Soviet aid.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental precaution is not in the sources.

collective-defense.rationale: Lumumba opposed alliance blocs through positive neutralism, but collective defence as a principle is not discussed.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Self-determination implies annexation without consent is illegitimate.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Mobutu curbed the churches and recognised only four, though Lumumba did not.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; Mobutu was a partisan head of state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Lumumba's government sought to end Katanga's and Kasai's secessions, and national unity is called his legacy.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Opposed to regionalism and in favour of a uniform centralised state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Mobutu was celebrated as father of the nation but not as divine; the tradition is republican.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax rate structure is not in the sources on Congolese nationalism.

character-from-environment.rationale: The speech blames colonial conditions for degradation; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Lumumba promised rule by law and consent, not unaccountable power.

space-expansion.rationale: Space is irrelevant to the nationalist program in the sources.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed government is not part of the documented doctrine.

leader-cult.rationale: Mobutu was officially glorified as father of the nation and the ideology was glorified by his officials; Lumumbists also revered Lumumba as martyr.

equal-parenting.rationale: Child custody law is not addressed in the sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Congolese nationalism is not a socialist doctrine in the sources, so the question does not apply.

land-redistribution.rationale: Protecting land for Congolese implies reallocation to them, but not documented.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Congolese nationalism accepts the colonial borders; claims over ethnic kin elsewhere are not part of it.

women-must-cover.rationale: Authenticité prescribed a dress code, but no covering for women.

common-currency.rationale: Lumumba and Nkrumah's Union of African States is documented, but a shared currency is not.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-Africanism and a Union of African States with Nkrumah were part of Lumumba's aims.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Opposed to regionalism and tribalism in favour of uniform unity.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The question concerns diaspora minorities and has no counterpart in the sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is not documented as Congolese nationalist doctrine; Lumumbism is described as nationalism and humanism.

ban-cartels.rationale: The sources do not discuss cartels or competition law.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is not mentioned in the sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The sources do not say whether courts should limit national majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas are not mentioned in the sources.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Economic independence is stressed, but not a closed bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade-agreement standards are not discussed in the sources.

moral-incentives.rationale: Authenticité had an ethic of national duty but did not replace material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The MNC pursued mass nationalism and elections, not foco insurgency.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The speech opposes inequality and discrimination, and the republic rejected both colonial and customary hierarchy.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Authenticité sought to replace colonial perspectives with African heritage in culture and education.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The speech rejects colonial domination and its supposed civilising claims.

patriotic-education.rationale: Authenticité and nation-building promoted loyalty to the nation, flag and symbols.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Anti-discrimination stance, but no US-style preferences are discussed.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is absent from the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Capitalist crisis theory is not part of the documented nationalism.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The movement's whole purpose was ending Belgian dominance.

delink-world-market.rationale: Economic independence is sought but delinking is not documented.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This is a Marxist theory of imperialism not discussed in the sources on the movement.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Entrenched rights are not documented; the speech promised liberties without describing constitutional protections.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The speech frames the colonial order as illegitimate; Congo's borders were colonial creations that the nation nevertheless kept, so this is only partly applicable.

elective-rulers.rationale: Lumumba governed as an elected Prime Minister and promised consent-based rule.

minority-veto.rationale: The movement favoured unitary national decisions over regional vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The sources do not state a doctrine of resistance to rulers who break constitutional law, and Lumumba himself was removed by a coup.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Lumumba worked through parliament but clashed with the president; not a stated doctrine.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics are not in the sources.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not in the sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Duties of the privileged are not discussed beyond the speech's call for social justice.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Nationalism calls for active participation in building the nation.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Critical theory of mass culture is not documented in the sources.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is not documented in the sources.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The speech presents colonial rule as extraction through forced labour, and economic independence as a remedy; the global-structure argument is inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Africanisation of the administration was part of the MNC platform.

party-own-road.rationale: The question is about communist parties and does not apply directly to a nationalist movement.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The speech welcomes aid if freely given, but stresses national economic independence.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The sources show no claims by Congolese nationalists on lost territory.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Africanisation and Congolese rule of the Congo were central aims.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anti-fascism as a constitutional principle is not discussed in the sources.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The sources do not address the comparison of fascism and communism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American history is unrelated to the sources on Congolese nationalism.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not addressed; adherents honoured Lumumba but also renamed colonial places.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Men's issues are not discussed in the sources.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is not discussed in the sources.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Authenticité held that Western institutions did not fit Africa, and justified one-party rule by African tradition.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Mobutu came to power through the army, but no doctrine of guardianship is documented.

paid-care-work.rationale: Care work pay is not discussed in the sources.

filial-duty.rationale: Heritage emphasis suggests respect for elders; not documented.

office-by-exam.rationale: Examination-based recruitment is not documented, though Africanisation of the administration was an MNC goal.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic independence implies protection of strategic firms; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not discussed in the sources.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Binding mandates for delegates are not in the sources.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: State welfare orientation suggests public pensions; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: African customary tenure is part of heritage, but no doctrine is documented.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary budget control is not discussed in the sources, though Lumumba governed through parliament.

single-official-language.rationale: One national identity was sought, yet Congo has four national languages and French official; no doctrine documented.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land protected for Congolese people; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The legal test for discrimination is not in the sources, which address colonial discrimination in general.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumerism is not discussed in the sources.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Congolese nationalism is a victim of foreign interference.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The independence struggle opposed outside troops, and Belgium's intervention was resisted.

corporate-influence.rationale: Foreign company control during colonial rule was criticised, but no doctrine on lobbying.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Sovereignty concerns suggest support; not documented.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Birth incentives are not discussed in the sources.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on property purchases are not discussed in the sources.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employer-of-last-resort policy is not documented, though full employment would fit the speech's social justice.

democratic-peace.rationale: Democratic peace theory is not discussed in the sources.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: A state-building movement expects obedience to national law.

non-intervention.rationale: Lumumba's independence speech claims the country for its own people against outside control (s1), but he himself asked for UN and then Soviet intervention in 1960, so 'for any reason' overstates the position.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed in the sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not part of the doctrine and contrary to unity.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom-of-information rights are not in the sources.

local-production.rationale: Localist economics is not in the sources; the economic aim was national independence.

informal-organisation.rationale: The MNC sought a unified national party.

religious-nation.rationale: The nation is defined by shared Congolese identity across religions.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The speech rejects subordination to a metropole.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Opposed to regionalism; Katanga's secession was about keeping mining revenue.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: This is a communist distinction not found in the sources on Congolese nationalism.

defeat-communism.rationale: Lumumba turned to the Soviet Union and pursued positive neutralism, rejecting alignment against communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public service delivery models are not discussed in the sources.

religion-illusion.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; Lumumba was raised Catholic.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Capitalism's historical role is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Women's equality is not discussed in the sources.

socialized-care.rationale: Public childcare is not discussed in the sources.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Authenticité renamed places and people, but no language purge is documented.

treaties-binding.rationale: The question concerns indigenous treaties and has no counterpart in the sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The movement favoured a strong unitary state.

majority-settlement.rationale: Contrary to equality among peoples of the Congo.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Positive neutralism and non-alignment; the MNC was neither doctrine.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The question is about historical or religious claims to land and the sources show no such Congolese claim.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The sources do not discuss the Holocaust; rejection is inferred from the movement's humanist and anti-racist rhetoric.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not documented; traditional culture stance unclear.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Mobutu suppressed opposition while Lumumba called for constructive opposition, so the strands split.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The speech condemns colonial exploitation by Belgium.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: This is an Islamic doctrine unrelated to the sources on Congolese nationalism.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Direct participation in decisions is not in the documented program, though the MNC was a mass party.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectional theory is not in the sources.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Transgender recognition is not in the sources.

assisted-dying.rationale: Assisted dying is not in the sources.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Positive neutralism rejects blocs but is not a stance on left and right.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist alienation is not part of the documented nationalism, though the speech condemns forced colonial labour.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority rests on the people, as the speech has it.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Authenticité prescribed the abacost and curbed churches; no rule on religious dress documented.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Employment secrecy law is not in the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: The sources do not describe a social market model; economic policy was state-led development.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: A national army was part of statehood.

rich-first.rationale: Economic independence and social justice suggest preference for broad prosperity.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Lumumba pursued positive neutralism and non-alignment.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The republic rejects hereditary rule; Mobutu did not install his son.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutual credit is not in the sources.

property-franchise.rationale: Contrary to equality in the speech.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is not in the sources.

reification.rationale: Marxist theory of reification is not in the sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The sources do not link press freedom to ownership; Lumumba's government restricted the press itself.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule through published laws is not discussed, though the speech promised consent and an end to arbitrary suppression.

racial-franchise.rationale: The speech rejects racial discrimination, and independence ended colonial racial exclusion.

online-participation.rationale: Online deliberation is anachronistic for the sources and not addressed.

open-government-data.rationale: Publishing government records is not in the sources.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition assemblies are not in the sources.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Reform of religious doctrine is not discussed in the sources.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Military service by gay people is not in the sources.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Mobutu curbed churches but did not promote atheism; Lumumba was Catholic-raised.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Lumumba opposed ethnic and regional power-sharing in favour of unitary state.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not discussed in the sources, and Mobutu ruled for decades without them while Lumumba's tenure was too short to show a view.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not in the sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction risk is not in the sources.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Women in religious office is not discussed in the sources.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Marital authority is not discussed in the sources.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Voting rights for foreign residents are not discussed in the sources.

rent-control.rationale: Rent regulation is not discussed in the sources.

abolish-ip.rationale: Patents and copyrights are not discussed in the sources.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Mobutu's MPR drilled youth wings, while Lumumba's movement did not, so the strands split.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear basing is not discussed, though foreign bases in 1960 were opposed.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Sovereignty and Belgian bases (Kitona, Kamina) were opposed in 1960.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Formal genocide recognition is not discussed in the sources.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The speech condemns colonial exploitation of labour; inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Wikipedia article says Belgian rule created the Congolese nation (s3), but that is the article's view, not adherents'; Mobutu's authenticité claimed ancestral roots, so adherents' position is contested.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Constructionist theory of sex is not in the sources.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Feminist theory is not in the sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Lumumba is honoured as national martyr and hero of independence.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Politics as a cosmic struggle is not documented in the sources.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The question concerns diasporas and has no counterpart in the sources.

culture-before-state.rationale: Authenticité tied culture to state-building at once; state first.

god-not-male.rationale: Religious language is not discussed in the sources.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist theology is not in the sources.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Economic independence and Africanisation; Zairianisation transferred foreign firms to Zairians.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The sources show no wish to merge regions by people, only to centralise the existing state against ethnic regionalism.

independent-unions.rationale: Union independence is not discussed; Mobutu later brought unions under the party but Lumumba's view is not recorded.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Congolese nationalism is not a socialist doctrine in the sources.

second-chamber.rationale: The Congolese legislature had a senate in 1960, but the sources do not record the nationalists' view of it.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Confederations of towns contradict the unitary centralised state Lumumba sought against regionalism and federalism.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation is not in the sources.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Longevity research is not in the sources.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Untraceable payments are not in the sources.

online-anonymity.rationale: Online anonymity is anachronistic and not in the sources.

person-over-state.rationale: Humanism in Lumumba, state primacy in Mobutu; split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The sources do not state a doctrine of human spiritual nature, though authenticité cited ancestral tradition.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Centralist: regions' powers rest on national authority.

gm-crops.rationale: Genetic engineering is not in the sources.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban density is not in the sources.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Congolese nationalism sought one nation above ethnic and racial divisions (s3), which rejects organising politics by race; the claim is not discussed directly.

racial-pride.rationale: Authenticité encouraged African pride and cultural disalienation, but it is not racial; split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Congo's nation was built across many language groups.

communal-electorates.rationale: Opposed to ethnic or tribal politics.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Katanga and Kasai secession was seen as Belgian-backed partition.

free-public-college.rationale: Tuition policy is not discussed in the sources.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Pollution taxes are not in the sources.

future-generations.rationale: Intergenerational duty is not discussed in the sources.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Gendered political values are not discussed in the sources.

arms-reduction.rationale: Disarmament is not in the sources.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not documented; inferred from speech openness.

capital-controls.rationale: Economic independence suggests it; not documented.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Central state authority; Lumumba worked to bring Katanga forces under the central army.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Wage top-ups are not in the sources.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Economic independence at the global level; inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Lumumba wanted to take over and Africanise the state.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Natural capital accounting is not in the sources.

sacred-nation.rationale: Authenticité elevated the nation; Lumumba is honoured as martyr.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student debt is not in the sources.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The sources do not apply a colonial analogy to a rich centre exploiting regions, though Katanga's secessionists complained of this.

public-service-media.rationale: Independent public broadcasters are not in the sources, and both Lumumba's and Mobutu's governments controlled media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Religious perennialism is not in the sources.

farm-price-support.rationale: Farm price supports are not in the sources.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Nuclear arsenals are not in the sources.

workers-own-party.rationale: Independent workers' parties are not discussed; the MNC was a broad national front.

ban-fgm.rationale: The sources do not discuss female genital cutting.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Women's inheritance rights are not discussed in the sources.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Dialect and language naming is not discussed in the sources.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Environmental liability law is not in the sources.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Environment versus liberty is not discussed in the sources.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Sentencing law is not in the sources.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Language rules for immigrants are not in the sources.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Closed-shop law is not in the sources.

voter-id.rationale: Voter identification is not in the sources.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The sources do not say how doctrinal disputes should be handled in law, though Mobutu recognised only four umbrella churches.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The sources do not define democracy procedurally, and adherents split between Lumumba's parliamentary path and Mobutu's one-party model.

premarital-sex.rationale: Sexual morality is not discussed in the sources.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Internet shutdowns are anachronistic and not addressed in the sources.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Negative income tax is not in the sources.

women-suffrage.rationale: Universal rights in the speech; inferred.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Religion and women's oppression is not discussed in the sources.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Gender ministries are not discussed in the sources.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Homestead ownership theory is not in the sources.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: International criminal courts are not discussed in the sources, and sovereignty concerns would cut against them.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Scriptural literalism is not part of the nationalist doctrine.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Women's participation in indigenous self-government is not in the sources.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Defending a planned socialist state is a Marxist-Leninist matter not in the sources on Congolese nationalism.

indirect-election.rationale: Indirect council-based election is not documented for the movement.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: None of the sources on Congolese nationalism mention abolishing money or wage labour.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: No source records a Congolese nationalist position on central banking or free-market money.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The independence speech promises an end to all discrimination of every variety, which runs against a right to discriminate.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Congolese nationalism defends the colonial territory as one nation and treats secession as illegitimate.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the Lumumbist unitary state opposed to secession; territorial status is not left to local votes.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on development and economic independence, which favours prosperity over limiting needs.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the unitary, equal-citizenship nation-building against regionalism, which opposes limiting settlement by group.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not address conscription, and the state tradition treated military service as men's.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Authenticite called for a return to the ancestral African heritage, and Lumumba's tradition glorifies the land won back from colonisers.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Lumumba's tradition condemned colonial arbitrary violence, but Mobutu's regime ignored due process; strands differ and drug policy is not addressed.

close-ties-china.rationale: Congolese nationalism stresses non-alignment, which gives no lean toward China or the United States; the sources do not discuss it.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The movement defends the colonial territory as one nation and has not made kin minorities in neighbours a theme.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Economic independence is central, but the sources show no doctrine of equal ownership of resources with compensation; unresolved.

self-ownership.rationale: Lumumba's speech attacked forced labour and humiliating bondage, implying a right of persons over their labour; no doctrine of self-ownership is stated.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Tax policy is not addressed in the sources and adherents have no shared view.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Lumumba's equality programme favoured services for all citizens ending colonial discrimination; inferred, not documented.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Lumumba built a party (MNC) while Mobutu's single party and leader cult bypassed rivals; the strands split.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Ending colonial discrimination and privilege runs through Lumumba's speech, which implies opposing privileged business; inferred.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Unitary nationalism sought to overcome ethnic and regional divisions; opposition to religious-denominational lines is inferred from that.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Authenticite combined cultural return to African heritage with a modernising, developmentalist state.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Not addressed; authenticity stressed customary culture while Lumumba stressed equality, and adherents would be split.

national-resource-control.rationale: Economic independence from Belgium and control of the country's wealth is central to Lumumba's independence speech and platform.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The independence speech stresses ending exploitation and discrimination and building equality, which suggests outcomes matter beyond how wealth arose; inferred.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Lumumba's economic independence stress gives no documented view on a transaction tax.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Lumumba's speech condemned racial discrimination under colonial rule, suggesting adherents still saw racism as a main obstacle; inferred.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The speech condemns colonial laws that were not the same for Black and white, implying unjust laws lack legitimacy; the conscience wording is inferred.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Not addressed by the Lumumbist or Mobutist strands, and nothing in the doctrine points either way.

multipolar-world.rationale: Lumumba stood for non-alignment and Pan-African solidarity, which fits an order of several independent centres of power.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Lumumba's nationalism was anti-colonial rather than economic-theoretical, and the sources do not discuss value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Lumumba joined national independence with equality and welfare for ordinary Congolese; inferred from his humanism.

material-over-identity.rationale: Congolese nationalism stressed unity across ethnic groups and cultural authenticity, but also economic independence; the left-right framing barely applies.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Lumumba was a non-aligned nationalist and the Mobutu one-party state was anti-communist; neither built market socialism under a communist party.

missingStatements.text: Countries should drop colonial-era names and Western personal names and adopt their own cultural ones.
missingStatements.rationale: Authenticite renamed the country, rivers and cities and required Zaireans to drop Christian names.
missingStatements.declined: Niche authenticity-policy detail; too specific to Mobutu-era Zaire to earn a place in the bank.

missingStatements.text: A newly independent state should keep the borders drawn by its colonial rulers rather than redraw them.
missingStatements.rationale: Congolese nationalism defends the colonial territory as one nation and treats secession as illegitimate.

notes: Lumumbist and Mobutist strands diverge on one-party rule, press control and the churches; the first leans democratic-parliamentary, the second authoritarian. Sources are mostly encyclopaedic, so many answers are inferred and marked low.
